claims.explanation: Mitoxantrone is a topoisomerase II poison whose cytotoxicity is limited by drug efflux via ABCG2 (BCRP), which actively pumps mitoxantrone out of cells. Selectively killed lines are therefore expected to have low ABCG2 expression and intact drug retention, while resistant lines show high ABCG2 expression or stem-like side-population phenotypes. TP53 mutation is nearly universal across both groups and does not explain selectivity, but wild-type p53 may modestly sensitize via CD95/Fas-mediated apoptosis.

mitoxantrone poisons topoisomerase II alpha; higher target levels increase cleavage complexes (PMID 20534341)
wild-type p53 upregulates CD95/Fas and mediates apoptosis after mitoxantrone-induced DNA damage; loss blunts killing (PMID 9841917)
P-glycoprotein effluxes anthracyclines and can contribute to mitoxantrone resistance
MRP1 efflux transporter associated with multidrug resistance to topoisomerase inhibitors
p53 pathway activation promotes CD95 receptor upregulation and apoptosis after DNA damage (PMID 9841917)
Fas receptor upregulation is required for p53-dependent apoptosis after mitoxantrone (PMID 9841917)
homologous recombination deficiency may impair repair of topoisomerase II cleavage complexes
HR deficiency may increase sensitivity to topoisomerase II poisons
defective DNA damage response may enhance mitoxantrone cytotoxicity
ARID1A-mutant lines are enriched among least affected lines, suggesting chromatin remodeling loss reduces drug sensitivity
